content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; model fails to account for downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price drops, especially when sentiment is low — forecasts lag recovery.
- When sentiment is high and prices are rising, model often overweights the trend, leading to inflated 30d forecasts.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds onto upward momentum longer than observed in true outcomes.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is positive, especially in the first 10 days.
- After a sharp price drop, model delays correction and underestimates the depth of the fall — often misses the “bottom” phase.
- Sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +0.85 and -0.34) leads to erratic forecasts — model struggles to smooth transitions.
